note: ORPHAN Pro 26:14 — as a door turns on its hinges, so the sluggard turns on his bed.

dims.v: fruitless sloth — the lazy man turning in bed, all motion and no progress
the sluggard who turns on his bed as a door turns on its hinges — sloth that has motion but no progress, endless turning that goes nowhere, activity that never rises to action
the busy idleness that turns and turns yet never gets up or gets on

atsel (sluggard) — 'as a door turns on its hinges, so does a SLUGGARD on his bed' (26:14); the lazy man is all motion and no advance, hinged to his bed. He stirs endlessly and arrives nowhere — the perfect image of fruitless sloth.
